assessments.reasoning: The GEIH instrument collects variables that allow disaggregating female-headed and women-maintained household structures across several dimensions, though not all. Specifically: 1) de_jure_vs_de_facto is true because marital status (Capítulo E, Q11), spouse presence (Q12), sex (Q3), and relationship to household head (Q5) allow distinguishing de jure female-headed households (unpartnered/widowed/divorced/single female heads) from de facto female-headed households (married/partnered female heads whose spouse/partner is absent from the household). 2) unpartnered_mother_child_units is true because line-number linkage to mothers (Q5A) and fathers (Q5B) combined with individual marital status (Q11) and partner presence (Q12) identifies unpartnered mother–child units anywhere within larger or extended households. 3) women_maintained_by_provider is true because labor and non-labor income variables (e.g., Capítulo I Q17, Q48; Capítulo L) are captured for each person individually, allowing analysts to determine the primary income provider regardless of designated headship. 4) mother_child_unit_activity is false because consumption and food preparation variables (Capítulo C Q7) are captured strictly at the overall household level and cannot be linked to sub-household mother–child units.
